Maria / team — attaching our proposed DPA redline (DPA_Redline_karthik_20270420.docx). Major points called out in the cover below.

--- COVER HIGHLIGHTS (legal) ---
1) Roles: We confirm Redwood acts as Processor on behalf of DataWorks for customer data processed through the hosted inference API. We will include explicit role mapping in the DPA preamble and in Schedule A.

2) SCCs: We accept the current EC standard clauses (Processor addendum) with Redwood’s customary limited deviation in Annex II regarding emergency incident notifications and lawful access procedures. Those deviations are described in the redline; we note them in the exception log.

3) Subprocessors / Delegation matrix: We included a delegation matrix (see spreadsheet) and a proposed notification cadence for future subprocessor additions. For immediate deployment, the delegates listed in the matrix are the only ones we use.

4) Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA): See attached one-pager — high-level assessment concluding that for the categories of data in scope we rely on SCCs + contractual safeguards and technical controls (encryption, access controls, limited egress). The full TIA is controlled and can be shared under an NDA if you need deeper detail.

5) Exceptions: A small set of exceptions where DataWorks requested changes that materially broaden obligations (e.g., removal of liability caps, open-ended audit rights) are captured in the exception log at the end of the redline. We’re open to discussion but will need pragmatic mitigations (e.g., scoped audit windows, notification timelines).

Next steps I propose:
- Maria: review the attached redline and highlight priority items for your counsel.
- If there are 3–5 narrow exceptions, we can escalate those to procurement/security for compensating controls.
- If acceptable, we can route the final DPA for signature via DocuSign and link it into the Order Form.

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed cover. I’ve run the redline by our outside counsel; they have three narrow asks:

1) Subprocessor notification window — they want a 30-day notice written into the DPA rather than a ‘reasonable notice’ formulation.
2) Audit scope — they request a defined scope limiting audit to security controls relevant to the DataWorks dataset and a quarterly cadence maximum.
3) Annex II wording — a tweak to incident notification timing (24 hrs -> 48 hrs) for specific categories where immediate impact assessment is operationally impractical.

Two quick clarifications for Redwood:
- For the TIA, can you confirm whether logs containing user PII are retained beyond 30 days and whether they are excluded from analytics pipelines?
- On the delegation matrix, one of our security reviewers asked if the GPU hosting vendor is considered a subprocesser or an infrastructure provider not listed — can you confirm the vendor name and whether they handle plaintext data at rest?

We can take the redline and your responses into a focused call. Any of the proposed times on Tue/Wed (PT) still work — we prefer Tue 4/20 14:00 PT if that slot is available.

—Maria

Maria — thanks for the notes and the counsel feedback. Quick answers and the proposed path forward below.

Quick answers:
- Log retention: production logs that could contain user identifiers are retained for a maximum of 30 days by default and are excluded from analytics pipelines unless a customer explicitly opts-in for analytics retention; we’ll add this language to Schedule B.
- GPU vendor: the hosting provider is "Aurora Compute" (infrastructure provider). They do not perform application-layer processing and do not have access to plaintext customer content outside encrypted volumes; this is documented in the delegation matrix.

On your three asks:
1) Subprocessor notification — we can accept a 30-day written notice for additions that change processing scope. For emergency/critical security patches we will maintain a shorter operational notification but will provide retroactive notice and mitigation details.
2) Audit scope — we accept a scoped auditor right limited to controls applicable to the DataWorks dataset; we propose a quarterly maximum cadence and a mutually-agreed scope statement to be appended.
3) Incident timing — we will accept 48-hr notification for the specified categories; for tier-1 incidents where service impact is high we will preserve a 24-hr hotline notification channel.

Next steps I propose:
- Olga to incorporate the three negotiated changes into DPA redline and produce an updated exception log.
- Laura to prepare final role-mapping language for Schedule A and confirm the retention language for Schedule B.
- I will route the updated DPA to your team and, if OK, we’ll move to DocuSign routing.

Olga / Laura — can you confirm you can turn the updated redline around by EOD Mon 4/26 so we can keep the DocuSign window open next week?

Thanks everyone — if Maria is available I’ll block Tue 4/20 14:00 PT for a short legal sync; otherwise we can confirm a new slot.

Best,
